Good morning. Last week, an estimated 72,000 migrants began crossing into a tiny Spanish enclave on the tip of Morocco. Within 24 hours, most of them had headed home. At least 88 people died after attempting the crossing, according to local officials. This isn’t the whole story of what happened over the last week, but the facts are worth remembering.

At an emergency meeting yesterday, EU interior ministers sought to draw a line under Ceuta, insisting that the passport-free Schengen area had never been at risk from the arrival of migrants at this scale. Despite this, much of the media coverage has suggested that events in Ceuta represent a territorial threat to Europe, sparking calls for greater security across the region’s borders.

events.title: Germany: How weather extremes impact local agriculture

events.title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake

events.title: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters

events.title: Poland: Top court rejects recognizing EU same-sex marriages

events.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?

events.title: 'Loneliness influencers': Being alone brings in the clicks

events.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern and WAFCON

events.title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?

events.summary: Following the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride parade, the Christopher Street Day parade, politicians and security experts are demanding consequences.

events.title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics

events.title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?

events.title: Germany's Transport Minister Schnieder to asks Merz to remove him

events.title: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks

events.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know

events.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups

events.summary: The Salton Sea is drying up, worsening air pollution for nearby communities. Officials are racing to contain it, but for some families, it's already too late.

events.summary: Since millions of NSDAP membership cards have been made available online, many Germans have been surprised to discover that their ancestors weren't always as innocent as family stories had led them to believe.

events.summary: The Welsh singer was best known for the 1980s rock opera hit, along with other songs, including "It's a Heartache."

events.title: Is the Strait of Hormuz still Iran's trump card?
events.summary: Iran's latest attacks show it can easily disrupt shipping, energy markets and draw in Gulf neighbors. DW asks how much leverage Tehran really has over Washington and if its high-risk strategy could backfire.

events.title: Assassin's Creed: Why pop culture is hooked on pirates
events.summary: Pirates have captured our imagination for centuries. With "Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced," gamers can now head off on another pirate adventure. How has our concept of pirates evolved with pop culture?

events.title: The Australian tree supercharging global wildfires
events.summary: As Europe experiences another summer of extreme heat and wildfire warnings, one tree imported from Australia is coming under renewed scrutiny across the world: eucalyptus.

events.title: Brain tumors: New vaccine offers patients hope for more time
events.summary: A new therapy offers people with seemingly incurable brain tumors scope for hope: It could slow the progression of the disease and extend patients' lives.

events.title: Heat-resistant housing: How we need to adapt our homes
events.summary: In Germany, it is time to rethink and rebuild. Many apartments were not designed for heat waves. Fortunately, there are ways to adapt existing buildings to the changing climate — but air conditioning isn't the best.

events.title: US: Progressive Democrat El-Sayed wins key Michigan primary
events.summary: He could help the #Democrats swing the #US #Senate in the upcoming #midterms. Progressive Abdul #ElSayed just won a tight #primary race in #Michigan, against more moderate congresswoman Haley #Stevens.

events.title: How to enjoy the most complete solar eclipse since 1989?
events.summary: No matter how sharp your vision, you're going to need some special glasses next week… Wednesday August 12 will bring the most complete solar eclipse since 1989 – the moon will fully cover the sun. To fully appreciate the celestial spectacle,you will require dedicated spectacles. Bryan Quinn and our colleagues at France Televisions tell us how to pick the right ones.

events.title: Who is Abdul El-Sayed, Michigan Democrats' best hope at taking back the Senate?
events.summary: Abdul El-Sayed won the Michigan Democratic primary election to contest one of the state's two Senate seats. He is just the latest progressive upstart to upset the game plan of the Democratic party's centrist establishment, with a platform that focused on working towards universal health care and getting corporate money out of elections… His criticism of Israel too was a flashpoint in the campaign – representing a growing shift among Democrats against what many see as an apartheid state currently carrying out a genocide while dragging the US into unnecessary wars in the Middle East. His portrait by Bryan Quinn.

events.title: Israel resumes military strikes on southern Lebanon as Rome hosts peace talks
events.summary: Israel again fired on southern Lebanon on Wednesday, blaming Hezbollah for violating a ceasefire, as US-backed negotiations in Rome sought to end months of cross-border hostilities. Lebanon said at least one person was killed in the attacks, while Israel issued its first evacuation alert in weeks for a southern town, underscoring the fragility of the truce.

events.title: Woman arrested after four stabbed in London's popular Covent Garden
events.summary: Four people were stabbed in central London and a woman has been arrested in a suspected "mental health related incident", the Metropolitan Police said Wednesday. The stabbings took place around lunchtime in Covent Garden, a bustling area frequented by tourists.

events.title: Democrat El-Sayed narrowly wins high-profile Michigan US Senate primary
Leftist El-Sayed narrowly wins high-profile Michigan Democratic Senate primary
events.summary: Progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed narrowly won Michigan's Democratic US Senate primary, US media projected, handing the party's left wing a significant victory in a pivotal battleground state. The upset over establishment-backed Haley Stevens is expected to sharpen debate over the Democrats' direction on economic populism, healthcare and support for Israel ahead of November's midterm elections.

events.title: Outrage in Libya over a video of a woman being publicly flogged for adultery
events.summary: A rare video filmed on July 21 in Sabha, Libya shows a woman accused of adultery being sentenced to 100 lashes. Shared on social media, it has sparked outrage for various reasons: Some are appalled by the fact that the punishment was carried out in a public space, whilst others are shocked by the ongoing existence of a law on extramarital relationships.

events.title: Netanyahu pushes back against Gaza deal, saying will not withdraw from enclave
events.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pushed back on a recent deal announced by US President Donald Trump for the disarmament of Hamas. In a video posted to social media, Netanyahu said the Israeli army would not pull back from its current positions in the Gaza Strip until the full disarmament of Hamas... comments that appear to contradict the terms of an October ceasefire deal. What exactly did Netanyahu say, and what could this mean going forward? Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Jerusalem, Noga Tarnopolsky.

events.title: Theme park or political park: Did France's 'Puy du Fou' break Russian sanctions?
events.summary: Is one of France’s favorite theme parks a ‘Disneyland for Dictators,’ as The Guardian claims? The British paper has uncovered documents that indicate the French theme park ‘Puy du Fou’ continued working with a Russian oligarch long after sanctions on him were in place, in addition to ties with Vladimir Putin. Solange Mougin has more on the popular French destination, its expansion plans abroad and how critics say it is re-writing history.

events.title: Drone with explosive device found near Ukrainian cargo plane at German airport
events.summary: German authorities launched a major security operation overnight after an explosives-laden drone was found on the tarmac near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig-Halle Airport, forcing flight diversions and prompting the deployment of a bomb disposal robot. A cargo aircraft that aborted its landing also struck an unidentified object mid-air before landing safely.

events.title: Russian drone hits street vendor in Kherson, Zelensky denounces ‘safari’ attack
events.summary: Authorities in Ukraine say at least 17 people have been killed after the latest barrage of Russian missiles and drones. The overnight attacks were the latest in a series of large-scale strikes that have become almost routine this summer. According to Kyiv, Ukraine was unable to shoot down a single Russian missile. Ukrainian civilians are also being targeted, but through small drones. Kyiv says Russia is deliberately 'hunting' down civilians. More details with FRANCE 24 international affairs editor, Kethevane Gorjestani.

events.title: The era of the machine: Silicon Valley shows off humanoid robots
events.summary: For decades, humanoid robots belonged to the realm of science fiction. But today, they're one of Silicon Valley's hottest markets. According to consulting firm McKinsey, automation could transform up to 30 percent of all hours worked across the US economy by 2030. Dozens of companies are already developing robots that can interact with people and even help with everyday tasks. FRANCE 24's Pierrick Leurent and Valérie Defert report, with Wassim Cornet.

events.title: Ceuta appeals for aid as child migrant crisis becomes 'unsustainable'
events.summary: Spain's north African enclave of Ceuta has appealed for urgent government assistance after hundreds of unaccompanied migrant children overwhelmed its reception system following last week's mass border crossing from Morocco. Local authorities have warned that the situation is "unsustainable".

events.title: 'Terrifying': deadly Russian attack on Kyiv overwhelms Ukraine's air defence
events.summary: At least 17 people died in a brutal Russian attack on #Kyiv and its region, including eight at a railway station. While it managed to intercept most drones, #Ukraine failed to stop a single Russian missile as it struggles with a crucial shortage of #US-made ballistic interceptors.

events.title: Four-tonne piece of Space X rocket believed to have crashed on Moon
events.summary: A four-tonne piece of a SpaceX rocket is believed to have unintentionally crashed into the Moon on August 5, a collision that posed no danger to Earth but is expected to leave behind a lunar crater. While there is not yet official confirmation that the Falcon 9 upper stage struck the lunar surface, it had been expected to make impact at approximately 06:35 GMT.

events.title: Guatemala volcano eruption forces hundreds to flee ash, gas and lava
events.summary: In Guatemala, authorities have declared a red alert – the most severe danger warning – in areas affected by the eruption of the Fuego Volcano, located about 35 kilometers from the country's capital. The alert covers the areas of Sacatepéquez, Chimaltenango, and Escuintla, home to around 1.6 million people. Story by Charlotte Hughes.

events.title: Tibet fears erosion of cultural identity under new Chinese Ethnic Unity Law
events.summary: In July, China implemented a new Ethnic Unity Law, which aims to strengthen patriotism across all regions of the country, including those populated by peoples who are not part of China's dominant Han ethnic group. One such region is Tibet, where Mandarin has become increasingly visible as Han Chinese settlement has risen. Beijing says the law will improve national integration, but for Tibetan activists, it is another attempt by Beijing to erode local identity.

events.title: High-stakes Michigan Democratic primary pits progressive against moderates
events.summary: It's a fight between two Democrats over who will be the party's choice to try and win Michigan's Senate seat in November. But it is also bigger than that. The primary pits progressives against moderates – and is seen as a moment of reckoning for the Democratic Party on how to proceed in swing states for the 2028 Presidential election. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Washington, Fraser Jackson.

events.title: Embattled FIFA head Infantino holds emergency talks amid calls to step down

events.title: France: Royal Chapel opens for two months at Versailles Palace
events.summary: Following years of restoration, the royal chapel at the Palace of Versailles has opened its doors to the public for more than just private visits for the first time until September 27th. events.title: Ukrainian capital lit up by massive overnight Russian strikes, killing 17
events.summary: At least two people were killed and a dozen more wounded in a Russian strike on Kyiv overnight. Ukraine has also increased its long-range attacks on Russia, with a growing number of victims on both sides.

events.title: Rwanda's big screen moment: Historic Cannes win sparks creative boom

The achievement has lifted an entire local film scene now in full bloom: in Kigali, restored movie theatre, open-air festival and a new generation of filmmakers reflect this momentum.

events.summary: A deadly heat wave is gripping large parts of East Asia, bringing the hottest temperature on record in South Korea and complicating earthquake recovery efforts in Japan.

events.title: Trump calls Iranian leadership ‘extremely duplicitous’ after Tehran denies new talks will start Monday
events.summary: Iran said it wasn’t holding talks with the U.S. but was in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: U.S. agrees to pause attacks on Iran subject to ‘rapidly’ making deal, Trump says
events.summary: The deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending Tehran’s “nuclear threat,” the president said.

events.title: At least 86 dead after migrants rush into Spanish territory from Morocco
events.summary: Spain was scrambling Friday to contain a sudden border crisis after tens of thousands of people rushed into its North African territory, with dozens killed and political shock waves spreading across Europe.

events.title: Iran vows to ‘punish the aggressor today’ after U.S. unleashes ‘heavy wave’ of strikes
events.summary: The conflict appeared to draw in new countries, as Egypt confirmed that a drone hit two natural gas vessels at one of its ports.
